To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ends of the closed loops in the globular protein structure are spatially close but are situated apart from each other by about 30 residues in the polypeptides chain; they correlate with the locations and the topohydrophobity of highly conserved residues; these residues, called'mostly interacting residues' are the most buried at early stages of folding
the ends of the closed loops in globular proteins, which are spatial close to each other in the native structure, are separated by 25-35 residues in the polypeptidic chain.

the ends of the closed loops in protein structures are the locations of mostly interacting residues that are spatially close but are situated apart by 25-35 residues in the polypeptides, and these residues are the topohydrophobes in the protein families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description of the folding process of globular proteins as a sequence of steps, which can be predicted by the use of the topohydrophobics.
the identification and analysis of universal positions in globular protein structures, and with their possible involvement in the folding process.

the description of globular proteins in terms of the 'closed loops' of polypeptide chains and with the identification of the most important structural elements, which are crucial for the formation and stability of protein structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
'the ends of the loops are the beginning of the fold'.
the ends of the closed loops are the most likely places to find the'mostly interacting residues' that are responsible for the formation of the stable protein fold.
the universal positions are the ends of closed loops, which are crucial for the formation and stability of the globular protein folds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loop ends and the topohydrophobics are the most important positions for the folding of globular proteins.
the loop ends are the most likely sites for the first contacts in protein folding.
we have identified universal positions in globular protein structures and demonstrated their crucial role in the folding process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a universal set of topohydrophobics can be identified in the protein folds of different origins.
there are universal positions in globular protein folds, and that they are crucial for the formation and stability of protein structures.
the loop ends, the mostly interacting residues, the topohydrophobics and the hydrophobic clusters are all connected.
